problem:
Which of the following vector-valued functions are differentiable with respect to $t$ on $t\in (0,\pi )?$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨1+{t}^{2},\,-t+2,\,\sqrt{t}⟩ \\ h(t) & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
All of these vector-valued functions are defined for all $t\in (0,\pi ).$ 

A function is differentiable on the interval $(0,\pi )$ if and only if each of 
 its component functions are differentiable on that interval.

Let's now consider the functions one-by-one.

- We differentiate $f(t)$ to find ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since each component of ${f}^{′}(t)$ is defined for all  $t\in (0,\pi )$, we conclude that $f(t)$ is differentiable on this interval.

- Next, we differentiate $g(t)$  to find ${g}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t+2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,-1,\,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since each component of ${g}^{′}(t)$ is defined for all $(0,\pi )$, we have that   $g(t)$ is also differentiable on this interval.

- Finally, we differentiate $h(t)$ to find ${h}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{tan}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,{sec}^{2}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since the second component of this vector, $\operatorname{sec}⁡t$, is undefined at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$,  we conclude that the function $h(t)$ is not differentiable on $(0,\pi ).$

Therefore, the answer is:

$\,$ $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ only
